learn.title: Make a letter cancel
learn.body: Elimination adds the two equations so that one letter cancels. This works neatly when the coefficients are opposites, such as $+y$ and $-y$.

learn.title: Make them opposite
learn.body: If nothing cancels, multiply one or both equations by a number first. Whatever you multiply, multiply every term, so the equation stays true.
Substitution works well when a letter is already alone. Elimination works well when both equations are in the form $Ax+By=C$.

questions.prompt: Add $x+y=10$ and $x-y=2$. What do you get?
If the coefficients of a letter are opposites, \_\_ the equations to eliminate it.
questions.explanation: Opposites such as $y$ and $-y$ add to zero.

questions.prompt: To eliminate $x$ from $3x+y=10$ and $x+2y=5$, multiply the second equation by
questions.explanation: $-3x$ cancels $3x$ when you add. Multiplying by 3 would give $3x$ and $3x$, which do not cancel.
Multiply the second by $-2$: $-2x-2y=-10$. Add: $y=2$. Then $x+2=5$, so $x=3$.
Multiply the second by $-3$: $-3x-6y=-15$. Add: $-5y=-5$, so $y=1$. Then $3x+1=10$ gives $x=3$.

questions.prompt: A pen and a notebook cost 5 dollars together. Two pens and a notebook cost 7 dollars. What does one pen cost, in dollars?
questions.explanation: $p+n=5$ and $2p+n=7$. Subtract the first from the second: $p=2$. The notebook costs 3.
